correctness.rationale: For N=2n the characters give λ_k=2cos(πk/n)+(−1)^k. Cesàro averaging kills unequal energies, so Fourier orthogonality yields μ_q=N^(−1) times the number of ordered equal-energy pairs with k+l=q modulo N, using invariance of each energy class under changing sign. Diagonal pairs cover every even q. The opposite-parity equation is cos(πo/n)−cos(πe/n)=1. For a=2cos(πo/n), both a and a−2 are cyclotomic integers with conjugates between −2 and 2. Every conjugate of a−1 lies in [−1,1]. If nonzero its integral norm forces every factor to have modulus one, so a−1=±1; the zero case gives a=1. The a=2 case would make the odd index zero. For the remaining values, folding the indices into [0,n] gives o=n/2, e=n at n≡2 mod 4, or o=n/3, e=2n/3 at n≡3 mod 6. Restoring signs and adding modulo N gives respectively {n/2,3n/2} and {n/3,n,5n/3}, both exclusively odd. The congruences are disjoint, n=3 is included, and the complementary Fourier modes span the kernel. A separate exact test (exact_support_check.py) compared energy classes modulo Φ_(2n) and the resulting index sums for all 118 orders n=3,…,120. This is finite corroboration; the norm and Fourier arguments prove the uniform result. The uploaded verify.py was inspected, not executed.
